answer: Three stations fix each identity's position before weight counts. The scarce input is one physical anchor: a basalt post at a harbor berth, holding one key, its core scan on record. Challenges leave all three at once; replies must triangulate within 3 milliseconds to that berth, stations across the river, never in one line. One post holds one berth and one light-speed delay; it cannot cover a second coordinate. One anchor costs $150 once; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 posts, 1,000 berths, $150,000 in hardware. A mismatched core scan, or one key fixing two positions in a round, zeroes the round.
